video_title: LaVar Ball & T Cole REVEAL the Truth About LaMelo's PUMA Deal, Lonzo's Shoes & MORE!

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on his 27-year career in basketball and coaching
quotes.excerpt: I coached 25 years before we decided that it was time to close the school

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: How long have you been in the basketball world, man?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: Most of my adult life. So, 27 years. I coached 25 years before we decided that it was time to close the school, our prep program. And that was basically based off our relationship of where we were trying to build with what we were going for with trying to build the camp program and the grassroots.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on why he closed his prep basketball program
quotes.excerpt: I couldn't get my heart behind going in every day and getting parents to come in

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: Why did you decide to close the school?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: I couldn't get my heart behind going in every day and getting parents to come in to our program and telling them, hey, you're going to come to the prep program, send your kid from halfway across the country or the world even with international kids, you got to pay 20, 25,000 a year for the program, right? And then when I send you out of here, you're still paying 20, 30,000 to go to college because of the way scholarships and everything else have changed and it's changed to be such a business. So when your heart isn't in to something as much anymore and you don't believe in it, it's time to get away.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the financial burden of youth basketball
quotes.excerpt: the average family that doesn't play in a major circuit, they're paying 4 to 8,000 a year

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What is your vision for youth basketball?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: With youth sports, everything has become so monetized. It's so financially stressful on families. The average family that doesn't play in a major circuit, they're paying 4 to 8,000 a year to travel, food, everything else. That's the Aspen Institute that studied and they released it. If you're playing on the circuit, if you're playing on EYBL, the numbers are bigger. It's bigger. So that 4 to 8,000 isn't the fees you pay the AAU organization. That's coming out of your pocket at the door and everything else.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the unique model of his new basketball circuit
quotes.excerpt: we have the opportunity to offer a great majority of what we're doing for free

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What is unique about what you are doing?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: We have the opportunity to offer a great majority of what we're doing for free. We partner with a company and partner Jason White with Frit Fundraising, the digital fundraising, and they've been the fundraising company for the next pro circuit for the last few years. Jason has a vision a lot like mine and when we met, we were aligned. We're going to have three tiers to the circuit, so if you play in five tournaments or eight or whatever it is, you're going to have the opportunity to raise those funds digitally to pay for a great majority of it, hopefully all of it, which takes away from the cost. One thing that we're doing uniquely different is we're not charging at the door.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on providing opportunities for unsigned players
quotes.excerpt: we are having a division that is just for those unsigned kids

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What about the players who have already graduated?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: We are having a division that is just for those unsigned kids. So if you graduate in May and you still need to be able to play to try to find opportunity to continue to play for film or the opportunity for a coach to still see you, we're providing that as well. Nobody else has that opportunity for these kids out there. But our film is going to be uniquely different because of the highlight availability for it. All of our film will be free to our families that are part of the circuit.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on his health struggles and recovery
quotes.excerpt: 14 days I was in the state of Texas Heart Memorial Hospital

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: How many days were you in the hospital?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: 14 days I was in the state of Texas Heart Memorial Hospital. 14 days they went to my family, they told them, hey, time to pull the plug. 21st day, this is the true story, 21st day, they said, hey, we're going to have to take you to court over this. Who's paying for this? It comes to business, you know? So it really got down to the point where my family had to make that decision. And that that day I woke up.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on his professional history with Raymond Brothers
quotes.excerpt: the time he was working for Raymond Brothers, who was with Roc Nation

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: Tell me about the people you have worked with.

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: One of my former players was with me his whole high school career, like a son to me. Coach for me, he's got NBA ties and everything else. The time he was working for Raymond Brothers, who was with Roc Nation. And getting a haircut one day, Richmond, Indiana, at my long-time barber Billy Webster, four people in the barber shop. And the call came in and D'Angelo's picture popped up. Now mind you, he played in this city, they knew who he was. He said, hey man, answer the phone. I answered the phone on speaker phone. And the call was they were trying to get to LaMelo Ball. And they said, hey man, we want to talk to Melo. And they said, can you get us in touch with JJ?

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the origin of the LaMelo Ball Puma deal
quotes.excerpt: the Puma deal was written 100% to be a Triple B deal

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What happened with the Puma deal?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: I'll tell the story. If you remember there was a leak, there was a leak that came out that said there was a private jet involved and everything else. That was to get the motion moving. And I'm not going to say his name here. When he sees this, he going to be, you know, I didn't get his permission. My guy put that out there with his contacts. He led this whole thing from behind the scenes. He gave that person you don't want me to mention their name, the blueprint. And I'll just tell the world that the Puma deal was written 100% to be a Triple B deal. It was supposed to be written and mimicked in the form of the Jordan deal.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on his relationship with LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: he was a huge fan. And I'm going to tell the truth. I'm going to tell why I passed the call off to him

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: How did you get involved with LaMelo?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: He was a huge fan. And I'm going to tell the truth. I'm going to tell why I passed the call off to him. I'm going to be as honest with the world as possible. And I told you this the first time we got together. I didn't see it. I didn't see it because I'm like, damn, I'm really not in tune with you. I didn't know you at the time. I knew of you, but I didn't have a relationship with him. So I can't feel any way personal about how that went down. My part of that was my son, one of my former players, called me, asked me for a favor and I do it every single day of my life.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the truth behind the LaMelo Ball Puma deal
quotes.excerpt: the Puma deal was written 100% to be a Triple B deal

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What really happened with the Puma deal?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: I'll tell the world what they don't know. Right? So the Puma deal was written 100% to be a Triple B deal. It was supposed to be written and mimicked in the form of the Jordan deal. Right? Absolutely. 100%. And nobody can deny it, so the receipts are available. They are out there. The receipts are in existence. That Puma deal was written 100% to be the Triple B deal.

quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the negative media coverage of the Ball family
quotes.excerpt: the negative's going to always sell. And so that's to attack LaVar

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: Why is there so much negative coverage?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: The negative's going to always sell. And so that's to attack LaVar. And every time you poke your head out, every time you get in and you say I'm going to go do this or I'm going to go do that, here come the stories, here come the BS. I've been telling you this for the four years that I've been around. That's the part that I always see is but it's been four years, she ain't been around. So, I'm going to go ahead and hold on. I'm going to say this for the world to hear. Y'all business is y'all's business. Yes. Right, that's number one. Yes. Number two is, I've been around four years, Tina's not been around in four years. She's not been around in the home. I stayed in the home, I've been there, come and go. She's not been around in the home.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the power of storytelling in Nike's success
quotes.excerpt: Nike built what they built by storytelling. We had Bo Jackson, Bo Knows, Deion Sanders

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: How did Nike become so successful?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: Nike built what they built by storytelling. We had Bo Jackson, Bo Knows, Deion Sanders, all. Nike built what they built in that machine by the power of storytelling. Yes. Okay. What are you? A truth teller. You do it a little different. Yes, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. That's definitely. All right. Nike when when things changed and we then see the ability for the commercials or the series of the penny commercials and all that other stuff, it changed, right? Because everybody's not viewing things the same way. That phone is moving quick for these kids.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the lack of authentic personalities in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: personalities change. So now you don't see as many personalities as you used to

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: Are there still personalities in the NBA?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: Personalities change. So now you don't see as many personalities as you used to, right? Or they're not coming to light in the same way. So you really think about it and I'm not saying this because he's your son, how many real personalities are left? How many people can move a room like that? Right? How many people can move an audience? So there's a couple and they teamed them up with one of the coldest, like with with Ant.

quotes.speaker: T Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: T Cole on the importance of representation in basketball
quotes.excerpt: it's representation. It's who's working for you, who's putting it out there for you

text_blocks.speaker: LaVar Ball
text_blocks.text: What is the most important factor in a player's success?

text_blocks.speaker: T Cole
text_blocks.text: It's representation. It's who's working for you, who's putting it out there for you, who's trying to get you these opportunities, right? So the representation, we know for a fact, because it's come back from NBA people that said, it's representation. It's simply representation. Even when it goes down to the to the the snubs on the All-Star game, it's representation.

Y'all know one thing about the Ball family is they not going to come back and refute that, right? They not going to come and say nothing. They going to let it die and whatever let y'all say whatever y'all want to say. Y'all already know that.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Cole defends LaMelo Ball's status as a serious NBA player
quotes.excerpt: If LaMelo Ball is not a serious player, the NBA must be trash.
quotes.quote: I was upset with the comments, he's not a serious player. If LaMelo Ball is not a serious player, the NBA must be trash. The NBA can't have it both ways, you got to be trash. And the reason I say that is because this, if LaMelo Ball is not a serious player, when he's healthy, he is busting the league's ass. So either the league is not serious in itself, you can't be both. A healthy LaMelo Ball, you're getting your ass busted and it's facts.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Cole discusses the trade rumors surrounding LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: I knew what was happening. I said, LaVar, they going to trade him.
quotes.quote: Then what happened is they let this story leak out. He been in the league how long? Six years. And then we want to -- and this is when I knew what was happening. I said, LaVar, they going to trade him. They going to put this little raggedy, stupid story out, LaMelo said he wanted to be president. You know what Gilbert Arenas told the people? What? He wanted to be a pimp. Right? Gilbert turned out to be a hell of a player. But you never heard that come up.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Cole
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Cole criticizes the management of LaMelo Ball's minutes
quotes.excerpt: You set LaMelo in the middle of another All-Star run. You start playing with his minutes.
quotes.quote: When they get you in that area where they want to trade you, they want to devalue you, they want to do all these things. You set LaMelo in the middle of another All-Star run. You start playing with his minutes. You start doing all -- for what? He wasn't hurt. You not getting behind him. You not pushing. Why are y'all not saying nothing about him not being an All-Star? His management damn sure wasn't doing it. So y'all saying he not a serious player. If he not a serious player, what that say about the rest of the league that can't contain him?
